articles.title: Did Jalen Hurts ask the Eagles for a trade? Here's what we know about the viral claim
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles could be facing an uncomfortable situation with their franchise quarterback, Jalen Hurts.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles could be facing an uncomfortable situation with their franchise quarterback, Jalen Hurts. Rumors about his future have started circulating, with a viral social media post claiming that the Super Bowl LIX MVP has informed the team that he wants a trade.According to the claim, Hurts is unhappy with how Philadelphia handled his injury situation and is ready to move on from the organization. The post even suggested that his time with the Eagles is over, leaving fans wondering whether they could soon see the quarterback wearing a different NFL jersey.But is there actually any truth to these claims?Has Jalen Hurts really requested a trade?No, as of November 24, there is no credible confirmation that Hurts has formally requested a trade from the Eagles. The viral claim should therefore be treated with caution rather than as an official development.While the trade rumors remain unverified, Hurts is genuinely dealing with a major health setback. In October, the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, announced that further medical evaluations had revealed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning blood clots had been discovered in both lungs.The quarterback was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his left calf after experiencing discomfort following Philadelphia's Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.Following additional testing, doctors determined that his condition required treatment with anticoagulants, commonly known as blood thinners. The medical team also confirmed that he would not be permitted to participate in contact activities, including football, while undergoing treatment.Hurts was subsequently placed on injured reserve, with reports indicating that he was expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season.The Eagles and his agent described his condition as clinically stable and expressed optimism about his recovery, expecting him to make a full recovery without long-term effects.Eagles face scrutiny over how Hurts' injury was handledThe quarterback's diagnosis has also raised questions about how the situation was initially handled. Hurts had undergone medical evaluation before Philadelphia's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London and ultimately played in that matchup. The subsequent discovery of more serious blood clots brought additional attention to the decisions made during that period.The NFL and NFL Players Association have since agreed to have independent medical experts review the circumstances surrounding his diagnosis.That review has added another layer to the situation, although it does not establish that the Eagles mishandled his medical care or that Hurts is unhappy with the organization.Could Jalen Hurts really leave Philadelphia?There is a difference between trade speculation and an actual request from a player to leave his team. Philadelphia's long-term plans at quarterback could certainly become a subject of discussion, especially with Hurts facing an extended recovery period and questions surrounding the team's future.However, the viral claim that he has already informed the Eagles of his desire to leave remains unsubstantiated.For now, the biggest priority is Hurts' health and recovery. Whether the quarterback's future eventually takes him elsewhere is a separate question, and one that remains unanswered.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The NFL's quarterback carousel could lead to 53 different starters in first 12 weeks
articles.summary: The NFL quarterback carousel has been as busy as ever with Arizona and Baltimore using it at a staggering pace.The Cardinals just used their fourth starting...
articles.body:
The NFL quarterback carousel has been as busy as ever with Arizona and Baltimore using it at a staggering pace.

The Cardinals just used their fourth starting quarterback in as many games, with well-traveled journeyman Josh Johnson getting the nod against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday after an injury to rookie Carson Beck .

The run of quarterbacks started with Jacoby Brissett starting and getting pulled in a Week 8 win at Dallas and then his replacement, Gardner Minshew, going down with a season-ending elbow injury after one start.

The Ravens just completed their own four-game stretch with four starters at the game's important position with Tyrod Taylor, Lamar Jackson, Joe Fagnano and Brissett getting starts from Weeks 7-10.

That kind of quarterback change had occurred only two other times since starts began being tracked in 1950, excluding 1987 when replacement players were used for three games, according to Sportradar, with Arizona also doing it in 2022 and the original Dallas Texans in their only season in 1952.

The Cardinals and Ravens are two of nine teams in a nonreplacement player season since the 1970 merger to use four starting quarterbacks in the first 11 weeks of the season. Dallas was the last to do it in 2020.

There will be more changes at quarterback this week with the latest coming when Pittsburgh announced Tuesday night that Aaron Rodgers had been benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against Denver. Anthony Richardson is also set to take over in Indianapolis after Daniel Jones was waived and Tommy DeVito is expected to start for New England in place of the injured Drake Maye.

That would make for 54 starting quarterbacks this season, the second most since 1990 through 12 weeks. There were 55 starting quarterbacks in the first 12 weeks in 1999.

Home-field advantage was back to being a factor.

Excluding the game played in Mexico City between Minnesota and San Francisco, home teams went 11-1 overall for the best performance in any week by home teams since they went 12-1 in Week 7 of the 1998 season. Only the Los Angeles Chargers lost, falling 27-24 to the New York Jets.

Three of the home winners were underdogs with Washington beating Cincinnati , the New York Giants beating Jacksonville and Philadelphia beating Pittsburgh for their 12th straight home win in the cross-state rivalry since the Eagles lost to the Steelers in 1965.

The impact of home-field advantage has dissipated in recent years as teams have gotten better at travel and dealing with obstacles on the road.

Home teams went into last week with a losing record of 69-72-1 this season, excluding international games.

Titans defense in midst of a historically bad run

The Tennessee Titans haven't been able to stop any offenses of late and could become the first team ever to give up at least 40 points in four consecutive games when they take on Jacksonville this week.

The Titans allowed the Cowboys to score touchdowns on the first six drives last Sunday, marking the seventh time that has happened since 2000.

Dallas added a field goal on the next possession before scoring another touchdown as Tennessee became the first team since at least 2000 to allow points on 13 consecutive possessions in the same season. Jacksonville had three TDs and two field goals on its last five drives in Week 10. The streak only ended when Dak Prescott took a knee on the final possession of the 51-30 win.

That marked the third straight game that the Titans have allowed at least 40 points, following a 43-36 loss to Cincinnati in Week 8 and a the 40-23 loss to the Jaguars following a bye in Week 9.

They were the fourth team since the 1970 merger to give up at least 40 points in three straight games, with it last happening when Tennessee did it in 2004. Baltimore did it in 1981 and Cleveland in 1975 along with nine other times before the merger.

No team in NFL history has done it in four straight games.

Midseason trades help Brissett and Cousins reach good and bad marks

It's rare for quarterbacks to change teams during a season but midseason trades helped Jacoby Brissett and Kirk Cousins achieve some rare feats.

Brissett threw a touchdown pass in his second start since being traded from Arizona to Baltimore and became the seventh player to throw a TD pass for at least seven franchises.

Brissett also did it for Arizona, New England, Indianapolis, Miami, Cleveland and Washington. Ryan Fitzpatrick is the only player to throw TD passes for eight teams, while Brissett joined Case Keenum, Brian Hoyer, Vinny Testaverde, Gus Frerotte and Chris Chandler as players to do it for seven teams.

Cousins' feat was not one he wants to celebrate. He threw a pick-6 in Minnesota's loss to San Francisco on Sunday night after also throwing one against the 49ers in Week 9 when he played for Las Vegas.

Cousins became the first player in NFL history, according to Sportradar, to throw a pick-6 against the same opponent in a season while playing for different teams.

The Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs have spent most of the past decade competing for the top spot in the AFC, with the Thanksgiving night matchup the latest big showdown.

The Bills lead the AFC with a 9-1 record with the Chiefs one game back as the teams prepare to play in the regular season for the seventh straight season to go along with four playoff meetings in that span. No other teams in different divisions have played more than six times since 2020 in the regular season and playoffs.

The Bills come into the game on a six-game winning streak that has clinched them a ninth-straight winning season. Only nine other teams have done that in the Super Bowl era and all but one — Kansas City from 1989-97 — made it to at least one Super Bowl in that span. The Bills are looking to get there for the first time since winning four straight AFC titles in the 1990-93 seasons.

The Chiefs head into the matchup having won three straight games, all by at least 20 points to tie a franchise record. The last time a team did that four games in a row came in 2017 when Philadelphia did it on the way to winning the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Three years after suffering cardiac arrest during an NFL game, Damar Hamlin signs a new Under Armour partnership focused on the mental challenges young athletes face
articles.summary: Damar Hamlin is taking on a new role beyond football, along with Under Armour to support young athletes dealing with mental health challenges.
articles.body: Damar Hamlin is taking on a new role beyond football, along with Under Armour to support young athletes dealing with mental health challenges. The Buffalo Bills safety has joined the brand's Protect This Mind initiative, almost three years after suffering cardiac arrest during an NFL game. The program aims to help student athletes manage stress, pressure and emotional struggles, giving Hamlin a chance to use his own experiences to encourage young people to take care of their mental wellbeing.Under Armour Partnership Focuses on Young Athletes' Mental HealthThe partnership aims to help young athletes cope with the demands of sports, school and personal life. Through Protect This Mind, Hamlin will help promote mental wellness resources for students, coaches and athletic communities. The initiative encourages young people to talk about their struggles and seek support rather than feel they have to deal with everything on their own.The partnership also connects with Hamlin's own experience of returning to football after a life-threatening medical emergency. His recovery brought physical and emotional challenges, and his involvement in the initiative gives him an opportunity to connect with young athletes who may be dealing with pressure or difficult situations of their own.Hamlin's Family Background and Early LifeBorn on March 24, 1998, Hamlin grew up in McKees Rocks, Pennsylvania, near Pittsburgh. His parents, Nina and Mario Hamlin, played an important role in his upbringing. He faced challenges growing up, but his parents' efforts and sacrifices helped shape his determination to build a career in football.Hamlin remains close to his family and hometown. He has a younger brother, Damir, and has kept much of his personal life private. His connection to the community he grew up in is also reflected in his charitable work and efforts to support local children.From College Football to the NFLHamlin attended Pittsburgh Central Catholic High School, where he emerged as a promising defensive player. His performances earned him a place at the University of Pittsburgh, where he spent five seasons playing for the Panthers.He finished his college career with 275 tackles, six interceptions and 21 pass breakups. The Buffalo Bills picked him in the sixth round of the 2021 NFL Draft, with the 212th overall selection.Hamlin made his NFL debut in September 2021 and earned more playing time in Buffalo's defensive lineup. He made significant progress during the 2022 season, recording 88 tackles and becoming a dependable contributor to the team.Cardiac Arrest and His ComebackOn January 2, 2023, Hamlin suffered cardiac arrest during a game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Medical personnel immediately performed CPR and used a defibrillator to restore his heartbeat before he was taken to hospital. The incident shocked the football community, with teammates, fans and players from across the country rallying behind him.After recovering, Hamlin began working toward a return to football. Getting back on the field meant rebuilding his strength and confidence after the frightening experience. He returned during the 2023 season and received recognition for his comeback, including the PFWA Comeback Player of the Year award.Charity Work and Community InvolvementHamlin founded the Chasing M's Foundation in 2020, starting with a toy drive for children at his mother's daycare centre. Following his cardiac arrest, the foundation received an outpouring of public support, allowing it to expand its work.The foundation supports young people through scholarships, football camps, donation drives and community programs. Hamlin has also worked to raise awareness about CPR and the importance of having automated external defibrillators available, helping more people understand how they can respond during medical emergencies.Giving back has become an important part of his life, particularly in the community where he grew up. Through his foundation, he continues to create opportunities for children and support initiatives that can make a difference.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Allen has one major advantage over Patrick Mahomes ahead of Thanksgiving, and history backs it up
articles.summary: Josh Allen has enjoyed a statistical advantage over Patrick Mahomes in their meetings since 2020, but Buffalo's Thanksgiving clash with Kansas City
articles.body: Josh Allen has enjoyed a statistical advantage over Patrick Mahomes in their meetings since 2020, but Buffalo's Thanksgiving clash with Kansas City presents a different challenge. The Bills host the Chiefs at Highmark Stadium on Thursday night, with first place in the AFC at stake. Both quarterbacks have delivered big performances in this rivalry, although their postseason results tell a different story. Mahomes has eliminated Buffalo four times in January, yet Allen's overall numbers against Kansas City suggest the Bills quarterback has often been the more productive player when these two teams meet.Josh Allen has consistently produced better numbers against Kansas CityThe rivalry between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes has become one of the NFL's most closely watched quarterback matchups. They have faced each other 10 times since 2020, splitting those games with five wins apiece. However, the numbers show that Allen has found ways to make a bigger impact across several key statistical categories.According to StatMuse, Allen has completed 232 of 359 passes for 2,573 yards, 20 touchdowns and just four interceptions in those 10 meetings. He has also added 506 rushing yards and seven touchdowns on 100 carries.That combination of passing and running has given Buffalo an important advantage. Allen averages 307.9 total yards and 2.7 touchdowns per game against the Chiefs. His turnover numbers are also impressive, with just five giveaways across those appearances, including one lost fumble.Mahomes has put up strong numbers of his own. The Kansas City quarterback has completed 239 of 361 passes for 2,715 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He has also rushed for 267 yards and three scores on 53 carries.His average stands at 298.2 total yards and 2.2 touchdowns per game, with 10 turnovers, including eight interceptions and two lost fumbles.Mahomes has thrown for more passing yards, but Allen's ability to create plays with his legs has made the difference in their overall production. The Buffalo quarterback has also protected the football better. That is a significant part of why his individual record against Kansas City looks so strong.Mahomes has the better form heading into ThanksgivingAllen's historical advantage does not automatically make him the favorite on Thursday. Mahomes enters the matchup with considerably better recent passing numbers, and his November performances have given Kansas City another reason to feel confident.The Chiefs quarterback has recorded at least two passing touchdowns without an interception in four consecutive games. During November, he has completed 102 of 146 attempts for 1,235 yards and 13 touchdowns, posting a completion rate of 69.9%.He has also contributed 29 rushing yards on six carries. While those numbers are not particularly remarkable on the ground, his passing efficiency has been the bigger difference.Allen, meanwhile, has had a more difficult stretch. The Bills quarterback has completed 80 of 131 passes for 1,023 yards, five touchdowns and five interceptions this month. His completion rate stands at 61.1%.He has still provided value as a runner, recording 50 yards and three touchdowns on 18 carries. However, the five interceptions are a concern, especially against a Kansas City defense that has repeatedly made life difficult for Buffalo in important games.The contrast is difficult to ignore. Allen has the stronger historical numbers in this rivalry, but Mahomes has been more consistent in recent weeks. That could become an important factor if Thursday's game turns into a contest decided by quarterback efficiency.Buffalo needs Josh Allen's running ability against MahomesThere is another reason Allen's previous performances against Kansas City deserve attention. His running ability gives Buffalo an option that Mahomes does not provide to the same extent.Allen has scored seven rushing touchdowns against the Chiefs across their 10 meetings. Those plays have added another dimension to Buffalo's offense and made it harder for Kansas City to focus entirely on stopping his passing game.Mahomes has shown that he can hurt defenses with his legs, too, but Allen's 506 rushing yards in this matchup highlight the difference. Buffalo can use him as a runner near the goal line or when passing plays break down. That creates additional pressure on the opposing defense.Still, the postseason history remains a difficult subject for Bills fans. Despite Allen's impressive individual production, Kansas City has beaten Buffalo in all four of their playoff meetings since their first encounter in the 2020 AFC Championship Game.Thursday's meeting offers Allen another opportunity to change the conversation, even if it is not a playoff elimination game.With both teams competing for the top position in the AFC, the result could carry significant weight heading into December. Allen has the historical numbers, while Mahomes has the recent momentum and the stronger postseason record in this rivalry. For Buffalo, the challenge is to make sure its quarterback's individual advantage finally translates into another important win over Kansas City.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers could lose $2.5 million after Steelers make stunning benching decision ahead of Broncos clash
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a major change at quarterback ahead of their Black Friday meeting with the Denver Broncos, leaving Aaron Rodgers facing
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a major change at quarterback ahead of their Black Friday meeting with the Denver Broncos, leaving Aaron Rodgers facing an unexpected setback. Pittsburgh announced late Tuesday that Mason Rudolph will start at Acrisure Stadium, while Rodgers will be inactive despite not appearing on the injury report. The decision also carries financial consequences for the veteran quarterback. Rodgers has up to $2.5 million in playoff incentives written into his contract, but his reduced playing time could put that money in jeopardy as Pittsburgh changes direction after back-to-back defeats.Aaron Rodgers' $2.5 million incentives are now under threatAaron Rodgers' absence against Denver does not immediately rule him out of earning his playoff bonuses. However, the Steelers' decision makes his path considerably more complicated.According to details shared by Steelers Depot on X, Rodgers must play at least 75% of Pittsburgh's regular-season offensive snaps to become eligible for the incentives.“If you are scoring at home, the Aaron Rodgers contract includes up to $2.5 million in playoff incentives he can earn, all of which require him to first play 75% of the Steelers' regular-season snaps. #Steelers #NFL”The contract contains four separate bonuses worth $625,000 each. Rodgers can earn one for every playoff victory, covering the wild-card round, divisional round, AFC Championship Game and Super Bowl.He has played approximately 97% of the Steelers' offensive snaps through their first 10 games. Missing Friday's contest alone would not push him below the required mark. The bigger concern is what happens if Rudolph keeps the starting job for the remaining regular-season games.The 75% requirement covers the entire regular season, not just the games Rodgers has already played. Every additional week on the sideline would reduce his share of the team's total offensive snaps. Even if he meets that requirement, Pittsburgh must win the corresponding playoff games for him to collect the bonuses.For a quarterback who joined the Steelers hoping to make one more championship run, the financial setback could become another consequence of a difficult season.Steelers are unsure how Rodgers will respond to the benchingThe timing of Pittsburgh's announcement has raised another question. Head coach Mike McCarthy had backed Aaron Rodgers as the starter just a day before the team confirmed the change.NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Steelers were also uncertain about the quarterback's reaction to the decision.“The #Steelers do not know how Aaron Rodgers will react to tonight’s news,” Schultz reported. “‘I guess we’ll find out together,' a source said.”That uncertainty adds another layer to an already uncomfortable situation. McCarthy and Rodgers previously worked together in Green Bay, winning a Super Bowl before their paths eventually separated. Their reunion in Pittsburgh was supposed to give the Steelers an experienced leader for what Rodgers had described as his final NFL season.Instead, two consecutive losses have left Pittsburgh searching for answers. The Steelers are 6-4 after Sunday's 19-16 defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles, and their offense has struggled to produce consistently.Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions in 10 starts. His 86.6 passer rating is a career low, and he has been sacked 31 times.Against Philadelphia, he completed 30 of 44 attempts for 227 yards and a touchdown, but the Eagles brought him down five times. Pittsburgh managed only one touchdown before the final minutes.Rudolph now gets the opportunity to change that picture. He has a 9-9-1 record across 19 career starts with Pittsburgh and Tennessee. The Steelers have not confirmed who will start after Friday, leaving Rodgers' immediate future uncertain and his playoff incentives dependent on a return to the lineup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers reportedly excused from Steelers facilities; benching decision unpopular with players
articles.summary: The Steelers were apparently still trying to make Aaron Rodgers happy early Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made the decision late Tuesday night to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers. On Wednesday morning, the team began dealing with the fallout from that decision.

Rodgers was reportedly not in the building early Wednesday when the Steelers held their morning team meeting at 8 a.m. ET, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor.

Additional reporting suggested Rodgers was excused from going to team facilities the day after it was announced he was benched.

At that meeting, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy officially announced the quarterback change to the rest of the team. That decision was reportedly "not a popular" one within the locker room, per The Athletic.

While Rodgers struggled this season, he was still well-liked by his teammates, per Pryor.

As for what led to Rodgers' benching, there's no specific smoking gun just yet. Some early reports Wednesday suggested the team was still working to make Rodgers happy early Tuesday. The Steelers were reportedly prepared to tweak the play-calling process at Rodgers' behest.

While it's unclear what changed Tuesday, the situation has reportedly been " brewing for a while ," per the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. Rodgers has, at times, been outspoken this season about the way the Steelers were run, but his comments about the team's front office and wideout Max Hurleman reportedly did not heavily factor into the decision to bench the 42-year-old, per Pryor.

After Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Rodgers sang the praises of Hurleman, who was elevated from the practice squad ahead of the game. Rodgers said players believed Hurleman did enough in training camp to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster and that his performance — he caught six passes for 61 yards and scored a touchdown — was a good reminder to the front office that Hurleman can play.

Pryor also reported things between Rodgers and McCarthy have been "tense" for a while . That was on display during an October loss to the Cleveland Browns, in which both men engaged in a profane back-and-forth during the game. McCarthy attempted to downplay that exchange after the contest, saying that's bound to happen when you've had a long relationship with a player.

The entire sequence is reminiscent of Rodgers' final season with McCarthy in Green Bay. After the pair split, reports emerged suggesting Rodgers and McCarthy were at odds during the season. But with Rodgers still playing at an elite level, it was much easier for the team to fire McCarthy and move forward with a different head coach.

Rodgers stuck around in Green Bay for four more years before he was traded to the New York Jets.

Any chance of Rodgers playing for another team in 2026 seems unlikely … for now. The Steelers reportedly have no desire to release Rodgers, who will be inactive for Friday's game.

Given Rodgers' declaration that 2026 will be his final season in the NFL, this could be the end of the line for the future Hall of Famer.

articles.title: NFL Thanksgiving preview: Bills and Chiefs renew a fun rivalry with big stakes in AFC playoff picture
articles.summary: The Bills are leading the AFC with a 9-1 record, and the Chiefs are a game behind.
articles.body:
No matter who else is in the AFC playoff picture, the Buffalo Bills will always have an eye out for the Kansas City Chiefs.

Since Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen entered the NFL, the Chiefs and Bills have met four times in the playoffs. Allen and the Bills have lost all four times. Allen hasn't made a Super Bowl yet despite having a great career, and the biggest reason is Kansas City has stood in the way.

The Chiefs had a stunning 6-11 record last season but have bounced right back. They're 8-2 to start this season. But the Bills are 9-1, and can practically knock one team out of its way in the race for the No. 1 seed by beating the Chiefs on Thursday.

The big question for the Chiefs was if Kenneth Walker III could return from a groin injury, abut the Chiefs ruled him out on Wednesday. Rookie Emmett Johnson has played very well in his place, but Walker was one of the best backs in the NFL for the first half of the season. The Chiefs could miss him in a huge game.

Johnson playing well is important because there could be bad weather. The forecast is for about 37 degrees with a 75% chance of rain at kickoff. There's also expected to be 19 mph winds, which could affect passing games.

The Bills will be looking to ride Josh Allen for a big home win. With Allen, the Bills are 0-4 against the Chiefs in the playoffs, but 5-1 in the regular season against Kansas City. Another regular-season win over the Chiefs wouldn't ensure that they could knock off Kansas City in the postseason, if the two teams meet again, but it would likely mean that matchup would be in Buffalo.

The Bills aren't getting endless shots at making a Super Bowl with Josh Allen. At some point this era will end, and it would be tremendously disappointing if it didn't include at least one trip to the final game. It's hard to think that far ahead, but this game is huge for the Bills in not only getting closer to the AFC's No. 1 seed but also making sure they won't be going to Kansas City in January. The Broncos, Jaguars and Bengals are all in the mix for the No. 1 seed, too, but the Chiefs have been such a problem for the Bills in the playoffs that it's OK to have a little more focus on being in a best position just in case they meet Kansas City again. The Chiefs don't want to fall two games behind the Bills and also lose ground on the Broncos in the AFC West, but this is a bigger game for Buffalo.

Downs has played just 28 snaps for the Chiefs since they acquired him in a trade with the Colts. But in those 28 snaps he has 10 targets, which is a great sign that Patrick Mahomes already trusts him and wants to get him involved. Downs has eight catches for 112 yards and a touchdown with Kansas City, which is tremendous efficiency for playing less than 25% of the offensive snaps in two games. The big question for this game will be if Downs is comfortable enough in the offense to take on at least half of the snaps in a huge game. Downs has already shown he can impact the Chiefs' offense, even without playing much. His role on Thursday will be a big story.

Vikings-49ers was billed as the Game of the Year last Sunday; hopefully, Chiefs-Bills lives up to the hype. Buffalo has been good to bettors overall (8-2 against the spread) and at home (4-1 ATS), while Kansas City has lost both games outright and ATS on the road against potential playoff teams this season (20-3 at Seattle, 28-24 at Denver). Patrick Mahomes has also thrown for 942 yards and 10 TDs (with no INTs) in Kansas City's last three blowout wins against less competition (NY Jets, at Atlanta, Arizona). Buffalo has won six straight — including the last four by at least 17 points — but still seems a little under-discussed for a 9-1 football team. Mahomes is an impressive 13-4-1 ATS as an underdog in his career. My gut says Josh Allen finds a way to get this done. He saves his best for Mahomes, Andy Reid & Co. — and this is the regular season, where Allen has dominated this matchup. The Bills (-3) cover another classic between these two great QBs. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

We're getting one of the NFL's best games of the year when the Chiefs travel to Buffalo on Thanksgiving night, though an ominous weather forecast (cold, rainy, windy) could affect the results. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you finish up the Thanksgiving slate.

1. Can Emmett Johnson do it again? The Chiefs wanted to get Kenneth Walker (groin) back after a two-game absence, but Emmett Johnson has been undeniably great as the temporary fill-in. Over the last two games he has 206 rushing yards and 108 receiving yards. He's in for another big workload on Thursday.

2. How much will Josh Allen run? Although Allen has continued to pile up the short-yardage touchdowns, his rushing production has been muted this year — he has just 51 rushing yards in the last five games, and he didn't have a single rushing attempt against Miami last week. The Chiefs have seen Allen plenty over the years, so they know how important it is to limit this element of his game.

3. What's the featured pitch in the Chiefs' passing game? Travis Kelce is coming off a two-score week, Josh Downs has hit the ground running with his new team, and Rashee Rice is a consistent factor on shorter routes. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around, so it's hard to view any of these guys as an automatic fantasy start. But there's a plausible upside for all three, as well. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers just left Mike McCarthy, Steelers in untenable situation
articles.summary: No matter what percentage of Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy are true, Rodgers' 30+-minute segment on ESPN railing against his longtime colleague who r...
articles.body:
If Aaron Rodgers had only accused Mike McCarthy of falling behind on film study and game preparation, perhaps McCarthy could have explained himself.

If the disgruntled Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback had only accused his head coach of breaking down the team with "1-2-3 Packers" rather than "1-2-3 Steelers," perhaps McCarthy could have laughed off the slip as a joke.

If Rodgers had only alleged that his play-caller fell asleep and snored in meetings or only alleged that his head coach said he did not need to ingratiate himself to defensive players or only alleged that McCarthy had missed walkthroughs, a franchise currently still on pace to make the playoffs could chart its next step more clearly.

Instead, as Rodgers scorched McCarthy with reckless abandon Wednesday on the "Pat McAfee Show," the four-time MVP left his coach — seemingly intentionally — with an untenable situation.

McCarthy is not in his second decade with the Green Bay Packers basking in the aftermath of the Lombardi glow as he once did when his tension with Rodgers boiled into the spotlight.

He's not several years into a Dallas tenure that featured three straight 12-win seasons as he was when Cowboys team owner and general manager Jerry Jones and McCarthy's disagreement over pay led to a lame-duck contract year and ultimate nonrenewal.

McCarthy doesn't even have a proven quarterback to call plays for the rest of the season, which by the way is coming fast as the Steelers host the Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

Stay quiet, and the Steelers know the NFL world — and likely beyond, as Rodgers' platform tends to stretch — will believe that Rodgers' allegations are at least partially true and McCarthy has lost his team. Multiple Steelers reporters emerging from open locker room Wednesday with sourced corroborations of Rodgers' account does not help McCarthy's case chalking this up to the latest Rodgers conspiracy.

Speak, and McCarthy faces overanalysis of any comments — not only from outside the building but mostly important from within. He's spent less than a year coaching his hometown team. This roster is not primarily rooted in young, impressionable players who have no comparison point for the work ethic and culture expected of an NFL head coach. Instead, players like 16th-year defensive lineman Cam Heyward and 10th-year outside linebacker T.J. Watt and 11th-year safety Jalen Ramsey all remember the culture longtime Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin established even as his ability to win in the postseason waned.

Adding to McCarthy's challenges: Rodgers built relationships with this locker room for an entire season before McCarthy arrived. It's Rodgers who fought alongside Heyward and Watt and tight end Pat Freiermuth to advance to the playoffs last season, and Rodgers for whom receiver Ben Skowronek bought a birthday cake nearly a year ago. It's Rodgers whom receiver DK Metcalf shared a bathroom with across two training-camp stints in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, and Rodgers who mentored the younger quarterbacks in the room even when McCarthy arrived.

"If we were a married couple in Green Bay, now we're an old married couple," McCarthy told Yahoo Sports in training camp when discussing Rodgers' presence in offensive meetings. "He talks a lot more now. I always thought I was a good listener, but I think I do more listening now. And actually it's really refreshing because to sit there and listen to him talk about footwork and just all the different things. And it's really good for the younger players. And I think Mason appreciates it, too."

McCarthy elaborated on Rodgers guiding veteran Mason Rudolph, 2025 sixth-round draft pick Will Howard and 2026 third-round pick Drew Allar.

"He is very forthcoming, particularly with Will and Drew, more Drew, just because Drew wasn't there last year. Will and Aaron have a very strong relationship," McCarthy said. "And obviously Aaron and Mason have a strong personal relationship, too. But yeah, I mean, footwork, reads, just particulars on a lot of plays."

It's Rodgers to whom the team was listening during training camp meetings — and Rodgers to whom the locker room was reportedly listening Wednesday from the locker room as the team's nearly-former quarterback aired his grievances on McAfee. The Steelers releasing Rodgers does not erase the impact of his words.

Rodgers' decades of complaints don't change McCarthy's résumé: He's won 60.7% of games across 19 seasons (180-116-2), advancing 12 times to the postseason and winning 11 of those games, including a Super Bowl. Even this season, the Steelers have a winning record and would advance to the playoffs if the regular season ended today.

But it's unrealistic to think McCarthy's credibility and reputation won't change after players listen to Rodgers publicize his allegations — some of which players are now telling reporters they have witnessed themselves.

Sure, Rodgers dabbled during his McAfee appearance in lines like "the only difference between conspiracy and the truth is time." The quarterback admitted that he wanted to call his own plays and demanded McCarthy at least give up play-calling, telling McCarthy to release him if he would not. The backdrop of all of this, of course, is a 42-year-old quarterback in the final year of his Hall of Fame career getting benched after leading the team to a winning record.

But as Rodgers' interview stretched on, and as he kept talking through McAfee's seeming attempts to wrap the segment, a truth became clear: No matter what percentage of Rodgers' allegations were true, and no matter how much of an axe viewers knew he had to grind, Rodgers' 30+-minute segment railing against his longtime colleague who remains the head coach of an NFL team will not be ignored.

McCarthy, along with coaches and players across the Steelers organization, find themselves in an untenable situation.

And hey, the Broncos will arrive in less than 48 hours with postseason hopes on the line.

articles.summary: Were the 49ers' and Bills' big wins enough to unseat the Bears in Tom Brady's power rankings?
articles.body: Tom Brady has dropped all sorts of fun quips in his NFL on FOX broadcasts this season. And as a Thanksgiving treat, Brady dropped another fun quote when he revealed his power rankings. Brady said that there's one quarterback in the league who is not only playing efficiently, but he's doing it so quickly that it's like listening to a podcast at 2.0x speed. He didn't say that about Josh Allen, Joe Burrow or Patrick Mahomes, though. Rather, Brady said Brock Purdy's the one who's playing the quickest and most efficient football. "He's just operating a lot faster than everybody else," Brady said of the San Francisco 49ers' quarterback. "Some guys are operating at 1.0. Some guys are operating at 1.5. Brock's operating at 2.0 right now. He's thinking fast. He's making fast decisions. The ball's coming out of his hands quickly. You know when you listen to a podcast, and it's at 1.0, but you speed it up to, like, 1.5 or 2.0? You just get so much more done." To Brady's point, Purdy has statistically been one of the NFL's best quarterbacks this season. He's ninth in passing yards (2,564), third in touchdown passes (23) and first in passer rating (118.2). He arguably had his best performance of the season this past Sunday, when he threw three touchdowns against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings' defense. Was that performance by Purdy and the 49ers enough for them to take the No. 1 spot in Brady's power rankings? Here's his full top 10. 10. articles.title: Cris Collinsworth is out for Browns-Raiders. Here’s who replaces him
articles.summary: Cris Collinsworth won’t call Browns-Raiders on Sunday Night Football. See why he’s out and who will join Mike Tirico in the NBC booth Sunday.
articles.body:
There will be a different voice in the booth when the Cleveland Browns host the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football." Cris Collinsworth will be off Sunday, with Jason Garrett replacing him alongside Mike Tirico, according to NBC Sports .

The change is part of NBC's unusual Thanksgiving week schedule. Collinsworth and Tirico will call the Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs game Thursday night. Tirico will then work Sunday's game with Garrett as the analyst, while Melissa Stark reports from the sideline, NBC Sports announced Tuesday .

It is not the first Thanksgiving week that Garrett has filled Collinsworth's seat. Yahoo Sports reports that this will be the fourth Thanksgiving week game Garrett has called with Tirico in place of Collinsworth.

Garrett is a familiar face to NFL viewers. The former Dallas Cowboys head coach now works for NBC and regularly appears on "Football Night in America." Yahoo Sports notes that Garrett coached Dallas from 2011 through 2019.

The Browns-Raiders game was not originally scheduled for prime time. The NFL flexed the Cleveland-Las Vegas matchup into "Sunday Night Football." The move gives Cleveland a national spotlight late in the season.

Sunday will also mark a rare moment for Browns fans. NBC says it will be Cleveland's first home "Sunday Night Football" game since 2019 . Coverage begins at 7 p.m. ET, with kickoff scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock.

articles.title: Detroit Lions to Alter Uniform to Honor Martha Firestone Ford
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have announced three ways they will honor longtime owner Martha Firestone Ford following her passing at the age of 101.
articles.body:
Thursday's Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Chicago Bears will carry additional emotional significance for the Detroit Lions and their fans. Following the news that longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford passed away at the age of 101 , the organization has announced several ways it plans to honor her memory.

The Lions previously released a heartfelt statement recognizing Mrs. Ford's dedication to the franchise and the city of Detroit. Now, the organization will pay tribute to its longtime matriarch both on Thanksgiving and during its next game in Atlanta.

Detroit Lions Reveal Plans to Honor Martha Firestone Ford

According to Justin Rogers of Detroit Football Network , the Lions will observe a moment of silence before Thursday's game against the Bears at Ford Field. Players will also wear a special helmet decal featuring Mrs. Ford's initials.

Here are the three tributes announced by the organization:

Moment of silence: Before Thursday's Thanksgiving Day game against Chicago.

Helmet decal: Players will wear an MFF decal during Thursday's game.

Jersey patch: A commemorative patch will be added ahead of Detroit's December 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Mrs. Ford served as the Lions' principal owner from 2014 through 2020 before handing control of the franchise to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp . As reported by NFL.com , she remained involved with the organization and continued attending games even during the 2026 season.

Thanksgiving football has always been special in Detroit, but this year's game will take on an even deeper meaning. It will provide the Lions and their fans with an opportunity to honor a woman who dedicated more than six decades of her life to the franchise.

Rest in peace, Mrs. Ford. Your presence at Ford Field will certainly be missed.

articles.title: Tony Romo, After Parting Ways With CBS Sports, Named ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ of Jake Paul’s Betr Betting App
articles.summary: Former NFL quarterback and football analyst Tony Romo has landed his next gig: He’s joined Betr, the sports gambling app co-founded by Jake Paul, as its firs...
articles.body:
Former NFL quarterback and football analyst Tony Romo has landed his next gig: He's joined Betr, the sports gambling app co-founded by Jake Paul, as its first-ever "chief predictions officer."

In the new role, Romo will serve as "a prominent face of the Betr brand," appearing in original content, delivering sports predictions and engaging with fans across the company's gaming products, including Picks, Predictions, Social Sportsbook, Social Casino, Arcade and Rips. As part of the agreement, Romo will become an equity stakeholder in Betr.

Romo, former QB for the Dallas Cowboys, had been an on-air analyst with CBS Sports since 2017. Last month, the network announced it was parting ways with Romo . That came after Romo had pleaded no contest to a charge of operating while intoxicated stemming from an incident that took place in Milwaukee in July .

Romo said: "I've spent my entire career trying to anticipate what's going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth. Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr." He added, "I'm looking forward to having some fun, making predictions and being part of where this company is headed. And I've got a pretty good feeling about what's coming next."

"Tony Romo has built an extraordinary reputation around something that sits at the very heart of our business: predictions," Joey Levy, founder and CEO of Betr, said in a statement. "His ability to see what's coming before anyone else has made him one of the most compelling personalities in sports, and we see a tremendous opportunity to bring that talent and personality to our growing ecosystem."

Romo joins Betr's roster of sports and entertainment talent partners, including NBA veteran Patrick Beverley, former Heisman Trophy winner Johnny Manziel and actors Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier .

articles.title: Mike McCarthy's Steelers Future Updated in New NFL Rumors as HC Addresses Aaron Rodgers' Release
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers reportedly have no plans to move on from head coach Mike McCarthy after releasing Aaron Rodgers following the quarterback's explosive interview on The Pat McAfee Show.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers reportedly have no plans to move on from head coach Mike McCarthy after releasing Aaron Rodgers following the quarterback's explosive interview on The Pat McAfee Show .

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Wednesday the head coach "has the full support of the organization" that is "standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes."

Rodgers previously told McAfee he had no plans to return to the Steelers and criticized the head coach for several mishaps behind the scenes.

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

As ESPN detailed, Rodgers said McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, had issues dating back to training camp, was reluctant to get to know some of the players, struggled with the game plan, didn't watch enough film and even said, "one, two, three Packers" in the locker room during Pittsburgh's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

For his part, McCarthy publicly spoke to reporters Wednesday shortly after the quarterback's release and said , "there were continuous efforts to reach Aaron," including reaching out to his agents, on Tuesday.

McCarthy added "there was an ultimatum made that was clearly out of his job description."

That contradicted Rodgers saying he heard he was benched from teammate Pat Freiermuth and had not heard from the coach.

McCarthy also said he made the decision to bench the future Hall of Famer, which was supported by ownership:

As for his job security, the coach told reporters he believes he is the man for the job "because I know how to win."

This is McCarthy's first season as the head coach of the Steelers, although he is 180-116-2 in his career with previous stops with the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys. The Steelers are also in the AFC playoff race at 6-4 but have lost two in a row.

Figuring out a way to stop that losing streak without the future Hall of Famer under center will be key, as the Steelers are just one game ahead of the New England Patriots for the AFC's final wild-card spot.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy Admits to 'Embarrassing' Mistake After Aaron Rodgers' '1-2-3 Packers' Story
articles.summary: On Wednesday, former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said during a tirade on The Pat McAfee Show that head coach Mike McCarthy led a "1-2-3 Packers" chant during halftime of a game this season.
articles.body:
On Wednesday, former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said during a tirade on The Pat McAfee Show that head coach Mike McCarthy led a "1-2-3 Packers" chant during halftime of a game this season.

Not long after, McCarthy confirmed to reporters the "embarrassing" gaffe:

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

Rodgers said during his interview that McCarthy had fallen asleep during meetings (or missed them altogether), was slow to watch film during the week and didn't attempt to establish a relationship with the defensive players.

But he said he felt the tipping point was the "1-2-3, Packers" chant.

"So, a lot of those [defensive] guys, he kind of already lost a lot of those guys. And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it, we're kind of on the offense on one side of defense on the other side. And there's some rambling or something, and without even a heads-up, he says, 'Alright, 1-2-3, Packers.' That's what he broke it down on in the locker room. It was one of those things where nobody was even saying Steelers because it was so in the moment, and it was like weird rambling. It was audible enough that everybody across the entire locker room heard it. I think we all looked around going, 'What the f--k... what is going on? Where's his head at this point?'"

Rodgers has since been released by the Steelers, and for now, the Steelers are backing McCarthy.

But reports are backing up Rodgers' claims.

Per ESPN , "One source told ESPN's Brooke Pryor: 'It's all true.' Another source confirmed to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo that Rodgers wanted to take over Pittsburgh's offensive playcalling but that McCarthy turned down the idea. A potential compromise was for quarterbacks coach Tom Arth to relay plays to Rodgers, at Rodgers' behest, sources told Garafolo. One source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that McCarthy 'crossed' Rodgers, leading to the quarterback's rant Wednesday."

It's all a mess, and it comes as the 6-4 Steelers attempt to end a two-game losing streak and keep pace with the Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) and Cleveland Browns (6-4) in the AFC North. Those efforts won't be easy with a Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos looming and a torrent of questions about what is happening behind the scenes.

articles.title: New Aaron Rodgers Rumors Update QB's NFL Future After Steelers Release, Comments on HC Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers officially released quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his explosive interview on Wednesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show, but the rest of the league reportedly isn't interested in the future Hall of Famer at this point.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers officially released quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his explosive interview on Wednesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show , but the rest of the league reportedly isn't interested in the future Hall of Famer at this point.

NFL insider Dianna Russini reported "there's no taker" among other teams before pointing out "injuries can change situations in an instant" even with "limited" options in the immediate aftermath of his release.

"Teams desperate on the playoff bubble, maybe, but it's going to be hard after watching him go scorched earth on people and an organization like that," an AFC team executive told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Rodgers shocked the NFL world Wednesday when he told McAfee he would not return to the Steelers and unleashed a number of criticisms on McCarthy.

Among those criticisms was Rodgers saying (h/t ESPN ) he learned he was being benched from teammate Pat Freiermuth and was yet to hear from McCarthy. The quarterback also said the coach fell asleep in team meetings, confused the Steelers for the Green Bay Packers in the locker room during the loss to the Philadelphia Eagles and didn't watch enough film.

Rodgers also said the coach was slow to learn the game plan.

Despite those comments, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Steelers fully support McCarthy and don't plan on making any immediate changes.

Pittsburgh faces the Denver Broncos on Friday and is one game ahead of the New England Patriots for the final AFC wild-card spot. While the AFC North team is a solid 6-4, it has also lost two in a row and now must adjust to life without Rodgers under center.

As for Rodgers, while there is no doubting his status as an all-time great, he turns 43 years old next month and is not exactly playing the best football of his career. According to Pro Football Reference , he is a mere 26th in the league with a 45.6 QBR.

That puts him behind the likes of Michael Penix, Malik Willis, Cam Ward and Kyler Murray, among many others.

Given his uninspiring play, age and tendency to draw even more attention to the team and locker room with his public comments, perhaps it shouldn't come as much surprise there aren't a number of teams reportedly knocking on his door with the hope of making a late-season addition.

articles.title: Greg Jennings Responds to Aaron Rodgers' Remarks on Mike McCarthy, Packers, Steelers in McAfee Video

articles.body:
On Wednesday, a benched—and since released—Aaron Rodgers appeared on the Pat McAfee Show and accused Mike McCarthy of sleeping during meetings, being slow to watch film and alienating the defensive players on the team, among his many remarks.

He also suggested those same issues dated back to his time coaching the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys. But former Green Bay wideout Greg Jennings said on First Things First that he didn't recall that happening during his time with McCarthy.

"None of us ever saw [McCarthy sleeping through meetings]," he said (6:00 mark). "... My time in Green Bay, I never experienced that. I never experienced any of that. I never knew there was chatter around it. And now when [Rodgers] talks about 10-plus years, I was there. Other guys were there. So then the texts started happening. I'm like, 'Did you see this? Did you?' I bore no witness to any of that.

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

Jennings, 43, played for the Packers between the 2006-12 seasons and, as he noted, the McCarthy he played under may not be the same version of the man that coached later in his Packers' tenure or time with the Dallas Cowboys and Steelers.

As you might imagine, former NFL players and former members of the Packers are already weighing in on the situation, with it dividing opinion:

As for the timeline of how we got here, the Steelers chose to bench Rodgers this week in favor of Mason Rudolph amidst a two-game losing streak. He responded by spilling the tea to McAfee and saying he wouldn't return to the team. The Steelers were clearly fine with a divorce, releasing him and putting their support behind McCarthy.

It was messy, and we'll likely be hearing plenty of excerpts about both men from former players in the days and weeks to come. Worse for the Steelers is that the players in the locker room will be left to answer a lot of questions about the divorce while trying to turn around their recent struggles.

articles.title: Top Landing Spots for Aaron Rodgers After QB's Dramatic Steelers Release
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers' pairing of Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has come to an end. The Steelers are releasing Rodgers, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' pairing of Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has come to an end. The Steelers are releasing Rodgers, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

The Steelers announced that they were benching Rodgers for Mason Rudolph late Tuesday evening. According to Rapoport, Pittsburgh had planned to keep the future Hall of Famer on the roster, but that plan changed after Rodgers publicly criticized McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show.

Among other things, Rodgers called McCarthy's approach to coaching this season "disrespectful to the game itself," per ESPN .

Rodgers will now go to waivers, and if he isn't claimed, he'll be free to sign with any team. Here, we'll break down Rodgers' situation, what comes next, and the most sensible landing spots for him if he chooses to finish out the season on the field.

When the season began, things between Rodgers, the Steelers, and their new head coach felt about as harmonious as they could be. McCarthy and Rodgers had a long history together and lifted the Lombardi Trophy for the Green Bay Packers.

Rodgers even stated that the hiring of McCarthy played a huge role in his decision to return for one final season.

It would seem, however, that things quickly went in the wrong direction behind the scenes. Cameras caught Rodgers and McCarthy in an unpleasant exchange during the team's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. According to Rodgers, the problems began long before that.

"I'm talking about in training camp when this stuff was going on, when he was missing meetings and the word was he's sleeping and then he's sleeping in the coaches' film sessions and he's not alert here." Rodgers told The Pat McAfee Show ( h/t ESPN ). "And he doesn't want to get to know the defense."

Rodgers hasn't played well in recent weeks, but his benching may have been about more than football. According to Rapoport , McCarthy "specifically" made the decision to turn to Rudolph at quarterback.

Only time will tell if Rudolph actually gives Pittsburgh a better chance to win against the Denver Broncos and moving forward. What's certain now is that Rodgers is leaving the organization. He's subject to waivers, since his release comes after the trade deadline, and he'll be free to sign anywhere if he isn't claimed.

Will Rodgers want to keep playing? That's unclear. He stated in the offseason that 2026 will be his final season. It wouldn't be a shock to see him finish out the season with another team, though, perhaps out of spite for McCarthy and the Steelers.

Would teams be interested in adding the soon-to-be 43-year-old? That may largely depend on how individual organizations view his latest slump. He's gone 6-4 this season but has completed just 60.9 percent of his passes with an 86.6 QB rating.

Teams will have to decide if Rodgers has been holding the Steelers' offense back, or if he's been hampered by bad play-calling and an underwhelming receiving corps. The truth may reside somewhere in the middle, but any team that wants him is free to put in a waiver claim now.

The Baltimore Ravens don't know when or if they'll have star quarterback Lamar Jackson back in 2026. He's currently on injured reserve with a thumb injury and was initially expected to miss up to 10 weeks, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

The Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett before the deadline after losing backup Tyler Huntley for the season to a turf toe injury. Brissett's presence makes it less likely that Baltimore would pursue Rodgers, but the pairing could be possible.

Baltimore has lost two straight with Brissett at quarterback, and Rodgers would probably provide an upgrade in ball security. If head coach Jesse Minter believes he can win with defense, a strong ground game, and efficient quarterback play, he could view Rodgers as an upgrade.

Brissett has thrown an interception in each game with the Ravens.

Rodgers' familiarity with AFC North defenses could also be an asset for the Ravens. For Rodgers, the prospect of facing McCarthy and the Steelers twice in the final month of the season could be extremely appealing.

If Rodgers isn't set on a revenge tour with the Ravens, the New England Patriots could be a very attractive destination. New England has slipped to 5-5 and appears unlikely to have starting quarterback Drake Maye back in 2026.

Maye is dealing with a fractured fibula that he suffered two weeks ago in Germany.

Since Maye got hurt right after the trade deadline, New England's top quarterback option is backup Tommy DeVito. However, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported after Maye went down that New England was expected to "explore the QB market."

Rodgers is now a part of that market, and his ability to read defenses, make smart decisions, and throw in rhythm would mesh with Josh McDaniels' offense. While Rodgers has no experience with McDaniels or head coach Mike Vrabel, he does have a history with receivers coach Todd Downing.

Downing was Rodgers' quarterbacks coach with the New York Jets in 2024.

While the Patriots have already played Pittsburgh this season, Rodgers could still throw a wrench in the Steelers' plans by joining New England. Both teams are currently battling to land a wild-card spot.

Rodgers' last game as a Steeler was Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Could he now switch sides and join the in-state franchise?

The Eagles are probably the longest shot on this list because they're rapidly falling out of the playoff mix. They're 3-7 and about to face a Dallas Cowboys team that routed them in Week 7.

Still, Philadelphia isn't out of the NFC East mix just yet, and it does have a roster capable of climbing back into the picture. The poor play of quarterbacks Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III was the biggest issue during Philly's four losses before the bye.

The Eagles have had injuries at other positions, but they've really struggled since Jalen Hurts stepped away to recover from blood clots. Rodgers could be viewed as a reasonable upgrade over McKee and Milton, one who could provide the Eagles with newfound life.

While Rodgers wouldn't get to impact McCarthy and the Steelers by joining the Eagles, he would get to play with the likes of Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert while trying to save a different franchise's season.

If Rodgers is simply interested in finishing his career with a playoff pursuit, the Atlanta Falcons would make even more sense than the Eagles. They're also sitting at 3-7, but that's not far behind the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers, who are 5-5.

The Falcons also have an impressive skill group, headlined by Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts. However, they've been held back by third-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr.

Penix has thrown seven interceptions, fumbled five times, and posted an 84.2 passer rating in eight starts. The top in-house options to replace him are Tua Tagovailoa and Andy Dalton, though neither has pushed Penix for the starting job since his return—Dalton signed as a free agent on October 19.

While Penix showed some promise immediately after returning from last year's torn ACL, he's only regressed since. He's made poor decisions, shown accuracy issues, and has lacked poise in the pocket. Rodgers' could help address these issues while fitting the offense of Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees.

Rodgers also has experience with Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt, who spent four years as his quarterbacks coach in Green Bay.

If a team doesn't claim Rodgers off of waivers, he's likely to bide his time and wait for a better opportunity to present itself—assuming he doesn't simply sprint off into the horizon instead. Such an opportunity would most likely come if/when a legitimate contender loses its starting quarterback to an injury.

Three teams stand out as top options for Rodgers should injuries create a quarterback emergency:

The Minnesota Vikings would probably be jumping at the chance to add Rodgers if they hadn't added Kirk Cousins just before the trade deadline. They have a top-tier defense and a bevy of talented skill players. However, they struggled mightily with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz behind center.

Should Cousins suffer an injury, Minnesota would probably become Rodgers' top choice. According to ESPN's Kevin Seifert , Rodgers "made it clear" that he wanted to sign with the Vikings in the offseason.

The Jacksonville Jaguars are looking to establish themselves as quality contenders in the AFC. The partnership between head coach Liam Coen and quarterback Trevor Lawrence has been a fruitful one since Coen joined the team last season, and Lawrence isn't getting benched any time soon.

Should Lawrence go down, though, Rodgers would make loads of sense. Backup Quinn Ewers wasn't even on Jacksonville's roster during the summer, and Rodgers has experience with receivers coach Edgar Bennett.

Bennett spent 13 years with the Packers and three seasons as Rodgers' offensive coordinator.

Should the Packers lose starter Jordan Love to injury, a homecoming would make tons of sense for Rodgers and for Green Bay. Rodgers' first stint didn't end particularly well, and he essentially forced the Packers to trade him to New York. However, he did spend four seasons under head coach Matt LaFleur and knows his offense well.

Rodgers won a pair of league MVP awards in LaFleur's system.

articles.title: Tom Brady's $2.2 million golf-course investment turned into a $200,000 loss before a $3.2 million sale
articles.summary: Tom Brady spent much of his NFL career making winning look effortless.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent much of his NFL career making winning look effortless. His success also opened doors to some of the country's most exclusive neighbourhoods. Yet one of his lesser-known real estate investments did not deliver the result he might have hoped for. In 2013, the former New England Patriots quarterback purchased a vacant plot at California's prestigious Madison Club. He sold it two years later at a $200,000 loss. The unusual part came afterwards. The same piece of land eventually changed hands for more than $3.2 million.Tom Brady took a $200,000 loss on his Madison Club propertyTom Brady purchased the 0.85-acre plot at the Madison Club in La Quinta, California, for $2.2 million in 2013, according to the Los Angeles Times. The exclusive golf community attracted wealthy buyers seeking privacy, luxury homes and access to one of the area's most prestigious courses.However, Brady did not hold on to the land for long. He sold the vacant property for $2 million in 2015, taking a $200,000 loss before accounting for transaction expenses.Unlike some of his other real estate investments, this purchase never turned into a sprawling personal residence. The plot remained undeveloped, leaving its next owners with an opportunity to create something of their own.For a property buyer, selling land at a loss is hardly unusual. Still, the transaction stood out because Brady was already an established NFL star with a growing financial portfolio. His decision also offered a reminder that even high-profile buyers did not always get the timing right in the luxury property market.Tom Brady's former golf-course land later sold for $3.245 millionThe story took another turn when the Madison Club plot returned to the market. In a May 14, 2019 report, the Los Angeles Times revealed that the property had been listed for $3.295 million.The land occupied an attractive position overlooking the fifth hole of the Madison Club golf course. Its location and surroundings helped make it appealing to buyers interested in building a custom luxury home.The asking price eventually translated into a substantial sale. On May 6, 2020, the Los Angeles Times reported that the property had sold for $3.245 million.That was more than $1 million above Brady's original purchase price and $1.245 million higher than what he received when he sold it in 2015.The later sale did not change Brady's original financial outcome, but it gave the property an interesting second chapter. What began as a relatively short investment for the NFL legend eventually became a multimillion-dollar land transaction.Brady went on to build an extensive real estate portfolio, including his high-profile Miami property. Yet the Madison Club transaction remained an unusual reminder that not every luxury investment followed the same winning formula.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Steelers officially release Aaron Rodgers and keep coach Mike McCarthy on the job despite embarrassing claims
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy keeps his Steelers job despite an ice cream assistant leak and Aaron Rodgers' claims he snores in meetings, saying "I know how to win."
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers are sticking with Mike McCarthy, but the embarrassment the coach must endure to stay at his post has not stopped since Aaron Rodgers pulled back the curtain on his failings – because other players have leaked unflattering details about the coach. The most bizarre leak is that Mike McCarthy has an ice cream sandwich assistant. You read correctly. AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS Former NFL veteran Breiden Fehoko, who played three years in the NFL and at LSU in college, posted on X that a Steelers player texted him McCarthy has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand. And that is true according to a source who confirmed it for OutKick and Fox News Digital. The coach has been seen getting ice cream brought to him and often greets the delivery with obvious satisfaction. 'WHAT THE F--K, CALL IT!': AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY CURSE AT EACH OTHER DURING HOT MIC MOMENT Despite that and other unbecoming claims Rodgers made about McCarthy on the "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, including that he falls asleep and snores during meetings, misses meetings and is generally "unwell," the Steelers are not firing McCarthy. They did, in fact, make official the release of Rodgers on Wednesday, which they didn't plan to do before his McAfee interview. But the club is privately confirming an ESPN report that McCarthy remains in his post and has the organization's full support. That was obvious once the Steelers made McCarthy available to reporters for a previously not scheduled news conference, a move that would not happen if he was being dismissed. In that press conference, McCarthy made a case for himself remaining as the coach. "I know how to win," McCarthy said. "And that's the facts. This is my third program. And I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization. We've got started and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today because of some of the things that, frankly, should have been talked about earlier. "So, this is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of it." McCarthy said he met with his player leadership council on Wednesday and came away convinced he remains the right person to lead the team as coach. "Yes, I do," McCarthy said. "And I will say that I just came from a, you know, player council meeting. I thought that it was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous, numerous things that have been underlined, comments that were brought to discussion to, you know, to the forefront. "So I'm proud of our leadership. I'll say that. And more importantly, I love the urgency that everybody had coming out of that meeting." McCarthy did not give a clear explanation why he decided to bench Rodgers in the first place, a move that led to all this drama. All McCarthy said was that Rodgers went outside the bounds of his job and that got him benched. "There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of his job description, so it was my decision to bench him," McCarthy said without adding detail. Despite this, the Steelers' player told OutKick and Fox News Digital he thinks Rodgers is more respected among his former teammates than McCarthy. But, he added, he understands why the decision to cut Rodgers was made. Publicly, players are paying Rodgers their respects. "This is something you never want to see," said receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling. "Obviously, we have a great relationship. He's one of my closest friends that I've made in this league. I wouldn't be where I am today without him." McCarthy was not asked about his ice-cream-fetcher. He was asked about claims Rodgers made. McCarthy admitted to some but refuted others. But McCarthy pushed back against Rodgers's claims that he fell asleep in meetings and missed walk-throughs, saying he took issue with how his commitment to the job was characterized. McCarthy also said it is not accurate that he holds a grudge against Rodgers for getting fired by the Packers in 2018. The problem McCarthy faces in all this is that Rodgers apparently has more credibility among players than he does – at least privately.
