articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Blasted by Former Packers Player After Mike McCarthy, Steelers Remarks, 'Despicable'
articles.summary: Former Green Bay Packers guard T.J. Lang, who was teammates with quarterback Aaron Rodgers for eight seasons (2009-2016), called his ex-signal-caller's remarks on their ex-head coach Mike McCarthy "despicable" during a chat on 97.1 The Ticket.
articles.body:
Former Green Bay Packers guard T.J. Lang, who was teammates with quarterback Aaron Rodgers for eight seasons (2009-2016), called his ex-signal-caller's remarks on their ex-head coach Mike McCarthy "despicable" during a chat on 97.1 The Ticket.

"I think it's despicable," Lang said in part. "I think Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has b---hed about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media.

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

"He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he was sick of it. Honestly, I don't even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It's just unnecessary. It's a victim mentality. It's a 'poor me, woe is me, oh, I thought this, and it wasn't that.'

"And I'm sick, man. I'm sick. I've been in a group chat with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do. I think it's just completely unnecessary. I think it's like what I said, victim mentality."

Lang further noted that he loves McCarthy, has a great relationship with him and talked to him on Monday evening. He also said he and Rodgers haven't talked in five years and that he can't remember the last time he returned a text.

On Wednesday, one half-day after he was benched and made inactive in favor of new Steelers starting quarterback Mason Rudolph, Rodgers launched a host of criticisms at his now-former head coach during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show .

Jomboy Media broke down some of the main talking points.

McCarthy was Rodgers' head coach with the Packers from 2006-2018. Rodgers was the Packers' starting QB over the final 11 seasons of that stretch.

The two reunited again this season after the Steelers hired McCarthy to replace Mike Tomlin, who stepped down after 19 seasons at the helm.

However, their reunion lasted just 10 games and ended in ugly fashion.

Now the Steelers forge ahead with Rudolph in hopes of holding onto a playoff berth. Their first post-Rodgers era game will take place Friday at home against the Denver Broncos. Kickoff is at 3 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers reveals why his $400 million NFL fortune made him fearless during explosive Mike McCarthy fallout
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is no longer interested in keeping his frustrations inside the Pittsburgh Steelers locker room.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is no longer interested in keeping his frustrations inside the Pittsburgh Steelers locker room. Just hours after Pittsburgh decided to bench him, the veteran quarterback delivered a stunning account of his troubled relationship with head coach Mike McCarthy. During a lengthy appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, Rodgers questioned McCarthy's commitment, preparation and leadership. He also explained why his estimated $400 million career earnings made it easier to speak openly, even if it meant ending his Steelers career.Aaron Rodgers uses $400 million NFL fortune to explain bold Mike McCarthy criticismRodgers made it clear that his decision to speak publicly did not come from a sudden burst of anger. According to the four-time MVP, concerns about McCarthy had been building for weeks. He claimed the coach had missed important meetings, fallen asleep during film sessions and failed to show enough interest in learning the defensive system.The quarterback also suggested that other people within the organisation were reluctant to raise similar concerns because they feared the consequences for their careers and families.His financial security, however, gave him a different perspective. Rodgers believes that having earned around $400 million during his NFL career means he no longer needs to worry about protecting his position at the expense of speaking honestly.Explaining his frustration, Rodgers said:"It should have happened earlier. We’ve had these conversations multiple weeks. Every time I bring up, “Hey, I heard you were sleeping in this meeting this week,” he says, “I’m not f**king sleeping. I never slept at the f**king facility. Who the fuck’s saying that? Fuck you.” I’m literally repeating things that these guys don’t have the nerve to say because they have a wife and a kid, only one year on their job, and they haven’t made $400m in the NFL.""Me, I don’t care. What are you gonna do to me? Like I said, you’re gonna release me? Cool. You’re gonna deflect this thing and make it look like you were trying to bench me and that I’m at home contemplating whether or not I’m gonna accept the benching? Couldn’t be farther from the truth."Aaron Rodgers rules out Steelers return after Mike McCarthy disputeThe comments also revealed how far the relationship between Rodgers and Pittsburgh had deteriorated. The quarterback claimed he had already asked the organisation to release him if it decided to bench him or allow McCarthy to continue calling plays.His remarks came after the Steelers announced Mason Rudolph would replace him as the starter against the Denver Broncos.Rodgers also described an uncomfortable moment involving McCarthy during the team's game against Philadelphia. He alleged that the coach ended a halftime huddle by saying, "One, two, three, Packers".For a reunion that once appeared central to Rodgers' decision to return for another season, the fallout has been remarkable. The quarterback has now made his position clear: he does not intend to return to Pittsburgh.Whether Rodgers finds another NFL opportunity remains uncertain. articles.title: Pat Freiermuth Addresses Aaron Rodgers Call, Steelers TE Told QB About Being Benched vs. Broncos
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Aaron Rodgers said during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show that he learned he was being benched from tight end Pat Freiermuth.
articles.body:
On Wednesday, Aaron Rodgers said during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show that he learned he was being benched from tight end Pat Freiermuth.

"I was talking to 'Muth and a couple other guys and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this,'" Rodgers said . "And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know. And he told me."

Rodgers Claims McCarthy Fell Asleep in Meetings

Rodgers: McCarthy Said '1, 2, 3 Packers' in Huddle

Shortly after, Freiermuth offered his side of the story.

"I was just checking in on a close friend, from what I heard," he told reporters . "That's all I have to say about that."

"Listen, anything I say about the situation, it's going to be tough, and obviously it's tough, but I'm here and we're just focused on trying to get a win against Denver," he added . "And obviously [Rodgers] said what he said, but again, I'm focused on the locker room and the team and that's really about all I have to say about that."

Head coach Mike McCarthy also offered his own side of the story:

"I was obviously here, we were going through game plan meetings, but I know there was continuous efforts to reach Aaron, and I know there was communication with his agents, so exactly the specifics of what happened on the other side of the conversation, I really don't have a comment on," he told reporters.

What followed was a tornado of messiness. Rodgers didn't show up to the team facilities on Wednesday, aired out his dirty laundry to McAfee, said he wouldn't return to the Steelers and was promptly released, leaving his teammates left to pick up the pieces amidst a two-game losing streak.

Peak cinema, no doubt, but an embarrassing day for a proud organization.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s parenting style takes a funny turn as his son reveals what happens during family dinners
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s lessons for his children do not always come at the right moment, at least according to his teenage son.
articles.body: Tom Brady’s lessons for his children do not always come at the right moment, at least according to his teenage son. The former NFL quarterback recently admitted that Benjamin, 16, has called him out for turning casual family dinner conversations into serious talks about life. Brady laughed at the observation during an appearance on Jake Humphrey’s High Performance podcast, acknowledging that his coaching instincts sometimes take over. The exchange offered a glimpse into how the seven-time Super Bowl champion approaches fatherhood, balancing his desire to guide his children with the need to understand their world.Tom Brady's coaching instincts often surface at the dinner tableTom Brady recalled how Benjamin recently described the pattern during a conversation at home. His son pointed out that a discussion could begin with something simple before his father suddenly made it serious.“My son said to me other the other night, he’s like, ‘Dad, sometimes we sit down at dinner and it’s just like a really easy conversation to start and all of a sudden you just get really serious,’ ” Brady shared. “And I’m like, ‘You’re right, Benny.’ Like, sometimes I do.”Brady admitted that his competitive background can influence how he responds to everyday situations. Rather than letting a conversation pass, he often sees an opportunity to share lessons he learned through years of playing football.“But, like sometimes that coach comes out in me and you know, I’m taking these things that [are] given to me and their lessons from their day, and I’m trying to say, ‘Okay, well, you’re 16 years old. I’m a little bit older than you. I was 16. I remember that. This is what I would do based on the 30+ years of experience that I have,’ ” he added.The former quarterback shares Benjamin and daughter Vivian, 13, with ex-wife Gisele Bündchen. He also has an older son, Jack, 19, whom he shares with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan.Tom Brady wants to understand his children's perspectiveBrady said being present for his children means more than offering advice. He tries to listen without judging them and understand what matters to them before sharing his own views.“I think a lot of it’s just that being really present for them,” he shared. “Non-judgmental, just trying to understand their perspective, but also trying to get them to understand my perspective a little bit too.”He also believes parents need to make an effort to connect with their children's interests rather than expect them to always follow the adults' lead.“The important thing for me in my personal life is to go where my kids are at too,” he explained. “I think it’s been a really important lesson for me over the years to go to my kids and say, what’s really important to you, what’s driving you, or what are you scared of, or how can I pay attention to the things that you value?”“So part of that is just being really open and present and also trying to be really relatable to the younger [generation], which I was very fortunate to learn over the course of my playing career.”Humphrey praised Brady's approach, joking that he would listen to a podcast called Parenting Tips with Tom Brady. The former NFL star, however, was quick to point out that he has not figured everything out.“Well, I’ve made a lot of mistakes.”“So, a lot like quarterback. I threw a lot of interceptions. And [at] every one I’ve tried to learn from,” he said. “And I’d hope I’m a better parent today than I was when I first started having kids. And hopefully I’m a better parent 10 years from now.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Josh Allen's numbers in 2026 have given the Buffalo Bills another reason to believe they can control the AFC, while Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City
articles.body: Josh Allen's numbers in 2026 have given the Buffalo Bills another reason to believe they can control the AFC, while Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs face a familiar challenge against their biggest conference rival. Their Thanksgiving matchup carries added weight, with Allen's recent production creating a clear contrast between the two quarterbacks heading into one of the season's most closely watched games. Mahomes remains one of the league's most dangerous players, but Buffalo's quarterback has built a strong case of his own. The matchup offers more than a rivalry showdown. It could shape the AFC's playoff picture.Josh Allen's rushing threat gives Buffalo a different edgeBuffalo's 9-1 record reflects a team that has found ways to win even when Allen has not produced his best passing performance. He has completed 194 of 302 attempts for 2,527 yards, 14 touchdowns and nine interceptions through 10 games. articles.title: How Micah Parsons’ return could give the Green Bay Packers a defensive edge in the NFL playoff race
articles.summary: Micah Parsons is finally back, and the Green Bay Packers could hardly have picked a better time to get him on the field.
articles.body: Micah Parsons is finally back, and the Green Bay Packers could hardly have picked a better time to get him on the field. The edge rusher is set to return against the Los Angeles Rams on November 26 after recovering from an ACL injury. Green Bay has managed to build a productive defense without him, but his presence could take the unit to another level as the playoff race tightens.The Packers have found ways to pressure quarterbacks this season, though stopping the run has been a different story. Parsons could help address that weakness without forcing defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon to change everything he has built so far.What Micah Parsons brings back to the Packers defenseParsons didn't need a full season to make his mark in Green Bay in 2025. Before his ACL injury in Week 15, he recorded 12.5 sacks, 79 pressures, 51 quarterback hurries and 28 run-stop tackles across 707 snaps. He also earned first-team All-Pro honors, making his absence a considerable loss for the defense.Green Bay has had to adjust since then. Under Gannon, the Packers have blitzed around 34% of the time this season, compared with 19.8% in 2025. The change has helped them get after quarterbacks, but the defense has struggled to contain opposing running games.Green Bay currently ranks 27th in rushing success rate allowed. Opponents have found room on the ground, particularly against a defense that regularly uses nickel formations. Parsons could help change that without requiring the Packers to send extra defenders into the box on every play.His ability to win battles off the edge gives the defense another way to disrupt offenses. Gannon could allow Parsons to attack the quarterback while keeping more defenders back in coverage, rather than relying so heavily on blitzes to create pressure. How Micah Parsons could help Green Bay push towards the playoffsThe Packers aren't exactly struggling to get to quarterbacks. They have recorded 29 sacks this season and rank fifth in the league in time to pressure, averaging 2.45 seconds. Still, adding Parsons to that mix could make the pass rush much harder to contain.His return could also benefit Lukas Van Ness, Dani Dennis-Sutton and Barryn Sorrell. Opposing offensive lines will have to account for Parsons, potentially leaving the other edge rushers with more favourable matchups. Gannon could also use different fronts and stunts to make life uncomfortable for opposing quarterbacks.Green Bay's three-safety approach, featuring Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams and Javon Bullard, has also worked well. Parsons' return doesn't necessarily mean the Packers have to abandon those combinations. If anything, it gives Gannon more room to use them while relying on his edge rusher to generate pressure.The Packers have already shown they can compete defensively without their star player. Now, they have the chance to see what that same unit can do with him back. If Parsons regains his pre-injury form, Green Bay could have a much stronger defensive foundation for its playoff push.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ $58.2M luxury property listings and $1.6M in small-business grants highlight his real estate holdings and charitable contributions in Northern California
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has listed three major properties in California, New Jersey and Wisconsin for a combined $58.2 million.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has listed three major properties in California, New Jersey and Wisconsin for a combined $58.2 million. The listings include his $39.5 million Malibu beachfront home, a $15 million New Jersey mansion and a Wisconsin estate priced at $3.7 million. Away from football, the four-time NFL MVP has also supported communities in Northern California. His COVID-19 relief fund helped 159 small businesses in Butte County receive nearly $1.6 million in grants, while his fire recovery initiative continues to fund local projects.Aaron Rodgers’ three luxury properties total $58.2 millionThe three homes reflect different stages of Rodgers’ NFL career, from his long spell with the Green Bay Packers to his time with the New York Jets.His most expensive listing is a beachfront estate in Malibu, California, priced at $39.5 million. Rodgers purchased the property in 2019 for $28 million while playing for the Packers. Realtor.com first reported the listing in August 2026.Located along the Pacific Coast Highway, the estate has a 4,625-square-foot main house with four bedrooms and a separate two-bedroom guesthouse. It also features ocean views, private beach access through a hillside funicular, a swimming pool and a spa.The property was purchased from British singer Robbie Williams and his wife, Ayda Field. Its renovated interiors include wood, concrete and Venetian plaster finishes.Rodgers’ second listing is a New Jersey mansion priced at $15 million. He bought the property for $9.5 million in June 2023, shortly after joining the Jets. The home sits near the border of Cedar Grove and Montclair and covers around 10,000 square feet.According to NorthJersey.com, the 18-room estate was listed on August 7, 2026. It has eight bedrooms, 9.5 bathrooms and sits on 2.39 acres of wooded land. The property also offers views of the Manhattan skyline.Its features include a wine cellar, cigar lounge, meditation room, media room and fitness area. Outside, there is a heated saltwater pool, sauna, spa and cold plunge. The property's annual property tax bill for 2025 was $71,369.His Wisconsin estate reflects his Packers yearsRodgers’ third property is a custom-built stone estate in Hobart, Wisconsin, near Lambeau Field. He purchased it in March 2015 for approximately $1.74 million and listed it for $3.7 million in November 2025.The 10,529-square-foot home sits on 5.32 acres and has four bedrooms. Its features include a home theater, fitness area, billiards room, greenhouse and outdoor sports facilities, along with a large kitchen and several living spaces.Rodgers spent 18 seasons with the Packers, making the Wisconsin property part of a significant period in his career. In 2025, he even joked with former teammates about buying the house.Before purchasing the estate, he owned another four-bedroom home in Suamico, Wisconsin. He bought that property for $442,500 in 2005 and sold it in 2017.The three current listings have a combined asking price of $58.2 million. This is the amount Rodgers is seeking from potential buyers, not money he has already received from completed sales.Aaron Rodgers’ COVID-19 fund supported 159 small businessesRodgers has also directed money towards community projects in Northern California, where he grew up. One of his major initiatives began during the COVID-19 pandemic.In February 2021, he partnered with the North Valley Community Foundation (NVCF) to establish the Aaron Rodgers Small-Business COVID-19 Fund. It was created to help locally owned restaurants and retail businesses in Butte County that were struggling with pandemic restrictions.Rodgers initially pledged $500,000 to start the fund before increasing his personal commitment to $1 million. The initiative also received additional support, including a $236,725 donation from Jeopardy! after he guest-hosted the show for two weeks in April 2021.The grants were distributed in two rounds. The first supported 80 businesses, while another 79 received funding in the second round. Together, the two rounds provided $1,599,967 to 159 businesses.The money helped business owners manage rent and other operating expenses when many were struggling to keep their doors open. According to NVCF, the first group received enough support to cover an average of three months of rent or longer. The second round distributed $578,000 among 79 businesses.Recipients included Pueblito’s, Great Harvest Bread Co., Bidwell Perk and California Regional Theatre. The grants gave local businesses additional support during a period when some were considering reducing staff, cutting working hours or closing.His Northern California fire recovery fund continues its workRodgers’ community support began before the pandemic. After the Camp Fire devastated parts of Northern California in November 2018, he contributed $1 million to establish the Aaron Rodgers NorCal Fire Recovery Fund.The initiative initially focused on helping communities recover from the disaster. Over time, its work expanded to include housing projects and programmes for young people.After six years of supporting Camp Fire recovery, NVCF shifted the fund towards an annual grant programme focused on the physical and emotional health of children and young people in Butte County.In March 2025, its first annual grant round distributed $215,266 among 12 organizations. Recipients included Berry Creek Elementary School, Paradise Recreation and Parks District and Berry Creek Rancheria of Maidu Indians. Their projects covered youth recreation, wellness activities and other community programs.The programme continued in 2026, with grants supporting schools, youth groups and local organizations working on children's health and activities. NVCF reports that the fund has distributed $1.9 million since it was established.There was also a major development in Rodgers’ playing career. On November 25, 2026, the Pittsburgh Steelers released the quarterback following his public criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers had previously confirmed that 2026 would be his final NFL season, bringing his latest chapter in Pittsburgh to an early end.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The decision came on Wednesday, Nov. 25, hours after Pittsburgh confirmed Rodgers would be inactive for its Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos. Backup Mason Rudolph had already been named the starter. Rodgers then appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and made a series of accusations against head coach Mike McCarthy, turning a benching into a wider dispute over the team's leadership.Aaron Rodgers accuses Mike McCarthy of falling asleep during meetingsRodgers did not hold back when discussing McCarthy’s conduct. The quarterback claimed the coach had repeatedly missed meetings and walkthroughs, while also appearing disengaged around the team.One incident stood out. Rodgers said McCarthy arrived late to a quarterback meeting last Wednesday, sat down and fell asleep within minutes.“Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes, began snoring,” Rodgers claimed to McAfee. “Woke himself up, was rattling his papers...five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened,” Rodgers said.Rodgers alleged that McCarthy then missed an offensive meeting the following day and did not attend the team's walkthrough on Friday, Nov. 20. He also claimed the coach missed a Saturday morning meeting.The quarterback said the pattern had been going on since training camp. His criticism was not limited to attendance. Rodgers described McCarthy as “unhealthy” and said the coach had struggled to build relationships with players.“He’s missing walkthroughs. You don’t think everybody on the field knows and is like, ‘Where’s he at? Why is he not here?’ ” Rodgers said.The comments raised questions about how much trust remained between the coach and his players. Rodgers claimed McCarthy had “lost” several members of the locker room and said many Steelers believed a change in leadership was needed.He also questioned McCarthy’s approach to the defense, saying the coach had shown little interest in getting to know that side of the team.“Mike didn’t want to get to know the defense. At one point I told him, ‘You should really lean into the defensive guys a little bit more and talk to those guys.’ And he said, ‘Well, I don’t think I need to.’ And I said, ‘Well, I disagree with that,’” the quarterback said.Aaron Rodgers says the Eagles loss pushed tensions over the edgeRodgers pointed to Pittsburgh’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 22, as a moment that deepened his concerns. He acknowledged the team had struggled and that its performance was poor.“The product wasn’t great,” Rodgers told McAfee.But he claimed the game also featured a mistake from McCarthy that proved especially troubling. Rodgers said the coach used the wrong team’s name during a halftime huddle, calling it the “nail in the coffin.”The quarterback’s own benching added another layer to the dispute. Rodgers said he did not hear the decision directly from McCarthy or the Steelers’ leadership. Instead, teammate Pat Freiermuth called him and revealed the news.Rodgers recalled replying, “‘Doing what?’”Pittsburgh announced late Tuesday, Nov. 24, that Rudolph would take over as QB1 for the Broncos game. The release followed the next day, leaving little room for a quiet transition.Rodgers, who joined the Steelers in 2025, had said he planned to retire after the season. articles.title: Rams DB Kamren Kinchens ejected vs. Packers for hit on WR Christian Watson, who's ruled out with a concussion
articles.summary: Kinchens was tossed for a helmet-to-helmet hit against Watson.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Green Bay Packers.

Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love was trying to float a pass to the sideline, targeting Christian Watson.

The Packers wideout looked over his shoulder to track the ball, and Kinchens came out of nowhere and laid a massive, unexpected hit on Watson.

He was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson, and the wide receiver remained down on the field, needing to be tended to by trainers. Watson was ruled out with a concussion.

Kinchens finished the first Thanksgiving eve game with just one tackle and two pass deflections. He will look to return next week when Los Angeles takes on the Kansas City Chiefs for "Thursday Night Football" next week.

This was the second injury Watson has dealt with in this game. On his first reception for 6 yards on the Packers' opening drive, he left the field and was questionable to return with a thigh injury. He returned on Green Bay's next possession.

Watson scored the Packers' first touchdown of the game in the second quarter. Love found him for the 6-yard score to help bring Green Bay within three points.

Watson has been no stranger to injuries this season. He left the team's Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers with a broken rib . Watson was taken to a local hospital during the game, but returned to the stadium in an ambulance, still wearing his gear, and ran back onto the field to return to the game.

The Packers wide receiver finished that game with 113 yards on six receptions.

articles.body:
The Packers entered Wednesday night's game against the Rams with the decisive wide receiver advantage as L.A. missed both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, but that advantage took a hit when Christian Watson exited in the first half.

Green Bay's breakout receiver absorbed a massive hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens and did not return, leaving Matthew Golden as Jordan Love's top target; Kinchens was ejected for the hit.

Watson was closing in on 1,000 yards for the season when he went down.

Here's what you need to know about Watson's status.

Watson was ruled out with a concussion after taking a hit to the chin from Kinchens late in the second quarter.

A stretcher was brought out for Watson, who remained down for a couple of minutes, but he was able to walk to the medical tent on his own. Unfortunately for the Packers, though, it was enough to leave him concussed.

In terms of Watson's availability going forward, the Packers are in a good spot with an extended break before their Week 13 game. Because Green Bay is playing on a Wednesday, there is an 11-day gap between the team's game against the Rams and a Week 13 battle with the Saints .

Watson, who has dealt with numerous injuries in his five-year career, memorably returned from the hospital mid-game and rejoined the Packers on the field during a game against the Panthers earlier this season.

articles.title: Steelers Get Blunt Take on Vikings Coach After Mike McCarthy Accusations
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores could be a name to watch this offseason head coaching cycle. Whether or not he gets a job remains to be...
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores could be a name to watch this offseason head coaching cycle. Whether or not he gets a job remains to be seen, but his name will be floated, and that's already starting.

Although the Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-4, the Mike McCarthy hiring is running off the rails after benching and releasing Aaron Rodgers.

Moreover, the veteran QB also aired out the issues with the Steelers' head coach in a flurry of accusations during his Nov. 25 appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show," one of them being McCarthy has been sleeping through team meetings.

If Pittsburgh does decide to move on from McCarthy after this season, especially if the team misses the playoffs, Chris Landers of FanSided floated several head coaching candidates, one of them being Flores.

"Steelers fans know Flores all too well, given that he spent a year in Pittsburgh as an assistant under Tomlin after being dismissed as the head coach of the Dolphins," Landers wrote in a Nov. 25 article .

"Why he's yet to get another shot at the top job despite his tremendous work in Minnesota has been one of the biggest questions of the last couple of coaching cycles; he's clearly one of the sharpest minds in the sport, and his tenure in Miami was hardly a disaster."

Brian Flores Would Bolster Steelers Defensive Identity

Moreover, Landers believes that Flores would bring back the brand of Steelers defensive football that has been missing this season.

The fact that several teams have sniffed around Flores before ultimately looking elsewhere is certainly a cause for at least some concern," Landers added in his article. "It's entirely possible that he's better suited to life as a coordinator rather than running an entire organization.

"Still, it's hard not to get excited about what he'd do with this defensive personnel, and he deserves a second chance eventually. From an attitude perspective, this feels like a perfect match."

NFL insider Ian Rapoport did report on Nov. 25 that the Steelers are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes. Still, missing the playoffs could cause this stance to change in the offseason.

Vikings Need to Improve O-Line Play in Week 12

Meanwhile, after the loss to the Niners, the Vikings will be looking to bounce back, and that includes Flores' defense. Nonetheless, former NFL offensive lineman Andrew Whitworth shared his concerns over the Vikings' offensive line ahead of their Week 12 game against the Atlanta Falcons .

"I think now you start to talk about offensive line issues and his lack of protection," Whitworth said during a Nov. 23 appearance on "Up & Adams." "There are a couple of snaps there where, literally, the second he hits his back foot, he has no time whatsoever to even think about where to go with the football.

"I think getting sped up and really struggling up front is just not a recipe for how they're going to have any success whatsoever. I don't care who's playing quarterback. So they've got to find a way to create some protection for Kirk. I keep saying this all year, the run game has to become more of what they do.

"That's always a staple in these kinds of offenses. Their challenge is going to be: How do we keep Kirk upright with more protection? How do we do things where we can run the football more successfully?"

articles.title: Rams starting linemen get hurt on back-to-back plays
articles.summary: The Rams lost Warren McClendon Jr. and Bill Murray to injuries on consecutive plays against the Packers.
articles.body:
The injuries continue to pile up for the Los Angeles Rams . During the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers , two offensive linemen went down on consecutive plays.

First it was right tackle Warren McClendon Jr. who suffered a leg injury. He was taken off the field with the help of trainers and escorted to the locker room where he was evaluated further. On the very next play, left guard Bill Murray was slow to get up and also had to be tended to by the training staff. He walked very gingerly to the locker room not long after McClendon was taken there.

It appears to be a lower-body injury for Murray, as well.

To replace the two starters, rookie Keagen Trost came in at right tackle and Justin Dedich, fresh off his activation from IR, took over for Murray at left guard.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Reacts to Brandon Aiyuk's Commanders Contract, Discusses Relationship
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels made it clear that he is "happy" to reunite with receiver Brandon Aiyuk, a teammate from his college days at Arizona State.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels made it clear that he is "happy" to reunite with receiver Brandon Aiyuk, a teammate from his college days at Arizona State.

Aiyuk is signing a practice squad with the Commanders after being released by the San Francisco 49ers after a tumultuous offseason. Now, Daniels is looking forward to getting the opportunity to play with the wideout again.

Aiyuk made news after calling out Daniels in an offseason post . However, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last week that Aiyuk "reached out to Daniels about a month ago to reconcile."

Daniels confirmed the two are on good terms on Wednesday:

That's good news for Commanders fans, as they will need the pair to have a good connection if the team wants to make a run at the playoffs.

Earlier this season, Daniels returned from his dislocated left elbow in Week 5 against the New York Giants, albeit with a sizable brace on his left arm.

The 2024 Pro Bowler received the necessary approvals to get back on the field. Still, his decision to put off surgery and only miss two games raised obvious concerns.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Oct. 11 that "there are doctors around the league who, despite not having examined Daniels, maintain that a player who dislocates his elbow twice — as Daniels has over the past 11 months — is at a higher risk suffering another dislocation, according to sources."

While Washington (4-5-1) remains in third place in the NFC East, the team has started to pick up momentum. It has won three of its past four games to get within two games of the first-place New York Giants.

Now, the Commanders are hoping Aiyuk can get up to speed quickly and re-establish a connection with Daniels to try to help the team make a run.
